title: Orbitline Activation Runway and Infra Handshake
next_steps: Redwood to share initial activation runbook and staging checklist
Orbitline to provide VPC peering IP ranges and SOC2 report copy
Schedule pilot bench (throughput test) for week of 2027-11-29
Set up SSO/SAML test account and grant Redwood service account access
action_items: Marcus: draft infra runbook + diagram and share by 2027-11-24
Priya: send VPC CIDRs + list of internal stakeholders by 2027-11-24
Avery: create kickoff ticket in Orbitline workspace and invite infra owners by 2027-11-23
Owen: share SOC2 type II and KMS policy excerpts (redact PII) by 2027-11-26
header: Date: 2027-11-22 | Time: 15:00 PST | Duration: 54 min | Attendees: 7 total (Redwood AE/SE/CSM + Orbitline Eng/Sec/CTO)
summary: Kickoff / infrastructure handshake for Orbitline Systems activation. Covered architecture requirements for private deployment vs dedicated, tenant mapping, VPC peering, SSO and KMS, pilot throughput target, and runbook ownership. Agreed on immediate next steps to exchange security artifacts and schedule bench tests.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena (AE): Alright everyone thanks for joining, we'll, uh, keep this tight — 45, 50 minutes ish to get the infra handshake and runbook sorted. quick intros?
[00:12] Priya (Orbitline): Hi I'm Priya, head of MLOps at Orbitline. we're owning infra and pilot timelines.
[00:18] Tom (Orbitline): Tom, platform eng, I'll be doing the VPC peering and routing.
[00:22] Lena: Marcus from Redwood here, I'll do the infra details and runbook. Avery from CS will own onboarding ops.
[00:28] Marcus (SE): quick note — we tuned the dedicated pool sizing based on your earlier perf notes, targeting 300 reqs/min with 95th p95 < 250ms for short conv gen.
[00:40] Sara (CTO): Is that for the hosted tier or dedicated? curious about isolation and disk encryption.
[00:47] Marcus: that's on a Dedicated pool we suggested. For Private (VPC) deployments we mirror that but you get full network isolation, customer KMS.
[00:55] Owen (Security): when you say KMS, are we able to bring our own HSM? and what's the key lifecycle?
[01:02] Marcus: yes we have integrations for cloud KMS and HSM-based key stores — but there's a configuration step in the runbook. we sometimes call it "bring-your-own-key" in the notes — we'll include the snippet.
[01:16] Priya: great — also we need tenant mapping guidance. we run multiple product teams, want separate model variants per team and separate logs.
[01:25] Marcus: understood. typical pattern is tenant-to-namespace mapping in the control plane; we can add RBAC roles per tenant, and you can pin model versions per namespace. we'll demo the mapping in the staging checklist.
[01:36] Lena: for the runbook owners, Marcus will draft infra diagram and steps, Avery will own scheduling and operational checkpoints.
[01:43] Tom: network specifics — we need to know which ports, egress allowed endpoints and what IP ranges Redwood needs to initiate peering. also, do you support cross-account VPC peering or do we need a transit/gw?
[01:56] Marcus: we support both. For cloud peering we can do direct VPC peering (cross-account) or via transit gateway, depends on your architecture. We'll ask for CIDR blocks and preferred mode in the questionnaire. minimal ports: 443 outbound for control plane, and a set of ephemeral ports for telemetry — we'll include exact list.
[02:15] Owen: encryption in transit — do you terminate TLS on your side? any mTLS options?
[02:21] Marcus: TLS termination happens at the edge but we can enable mTLS for private endpoints; mTLS setup steps are in the secure-comms section.
[02:30] Priya: timeline: we want pilot in early December; what's realistic?
[02:34] Lena: seems doable. if we get CIDRs, SOC2 doc, and SSO details by next Wed (24th) we can schedule bench the week of 29th.
[02:42] Sara: acceptance criteria for pilot? throughput? accuracy?
[02:45] Marcus: we'll define a small test harness: throughput ramp to 300 req/min sustained over 30 minutes with <= 5% error, token-level cost under agreed band, and functional eval on 3 canonical prompts to ensure quality parity.
[02:59] Tom: about logs and PII — what's redaction and retention policy? can we set retention to 30 days?
[03:05] Avery: in the console you get retention controls per route, default 90 days; we can set 30 days for your tenant and apply auto-redaction rules. we'll add the steps.
[03:14] Priya: ok good. also need a runbook section for model rollbacks and automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency spikes.
[03:22] Marcus: we have a fallback policy in the runtime — can be configured to route to a quantized variant. note sometimes the transcript in previous calls said "KV cash" — just to call out, it's "KV cache" — the runtime uses prefix and KV cache for latency wins.
[03:37] Owen: can we audit whenever fallback happens? we need audit trails for each request.
[03:41] Marcus: yes audit logs include model version, route, and reason for fallback. they can be exported to your SIEM.
[03:48] Lena: ok circling back — checklist items that must land before bench: VPC CIDRs, SAML metadata for SSO, SOC2 type II, and KMS policy excerpt.
[03:58] Priya: noted. who will own the test harness?
[04:02] Marcus: Redwood can provide a harness repo and a small k8s job to run the throughput test; we'll share parameters and a run script.
[04:10] Tom: what level of access does that require? service account?
[04:13] Marcus: we ask for a read-only cross-account role and a staging service account for push metrics. we'll include an IAM snippet.
[04:21] Sara: pricing questions — is the pilot billed as usage or a flat reserved?
[04:26] Lena: pilot is usage-based. If you commit to Dedicated or Reserved after pilot, we can convert and pro-rate. we'll include a pricing snapshot in follow-up.
[04:35] Owen: legal — NDA is already signed; procurement will request an addendum for data residency.
[04:40] Lena: we can support data residency in certain regions; will flag legal to coordinate.
[04:45] Priya: can we see a sample runbook?
[04:47] Avery: yes Marcus will draft and push to the shared drive; link will be in the follow-up email.
[04:52] Marcus: quick question — do you want model logs pushed to your S3 or to Redwood-managed logs?
[04:56] Tom: send to our S3 for compliance.
[04:59] Marcus: cool, we'll add S3 sink config and a sample lifecycle policy.
[05:05] Priya: ok last bit — tenant mapping: we have three teams (search, support, insights) — prefer separate model variants and quotas. any pitfalls?
[05:15] Marcus: quota enforcement is per-namespace. pitfalls: shared caches across namespaces would be avoided, and cross-tenant billing needs mapping to your internal cost centers — we'll show the account->tenant mapping in the runbook.
[05:28] Sara: what's the rollback SLO?
[05:31] Marcus: rollback should be under 5 minutes for a model route if auto-fallback isn't enough; full rollout rollback depends on canary speed. we'll document canary windows.
[05:41] Lena: recap — Marcus drafts infra diagram + runbook (due 11/24), Priya sends CIDRs and stakeholders (due 11/24), Avery creates kickoff ticket (due 11/23), Owen shares SOC2 + KMS policy (due 11/26). bench scheduled week of 11/29 pending artifacts.
[05:55] Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:58] Lena: thanks all, we'll follow up with runbook link and proposed bench calendar.
[06:02] Marcus: sending checklist and IAM snippet after this call.
[06:07] (call ends)

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" noted earlier) and speaker overlaps around 00:40-01:00 where SSO discussion had crosstalk.
